brands.d: New York family maker said to have put the first zip on a motorcycle jacket; created the Perfecto in 1928 and US Navy pea coats.
Oldest British motorcycle clothing company (D. Lewis Ltd); its Bronx of 1956 became the British Perfecto and the rockers' and punks' jacket.
eras: D. Lewis Ltd, Great Portland Street, 1929–1993

brands.d: South Shields maker of waxed cotton jackets with three royal warrants; the generic name for the wax jacket.
Stoke-on-Trent pioneer of waxed cotton motorcycle clothing, now a luxury heritage label.
Fall River, Massachusetts maker of hand-built motorcycle jackets and race suits with proprietary leather finishing.
Portland, Oregon custom leather shop founded by racer Ross Langlitz; the Columbia is its best seller.
Apparel line of Joseph Buegeleisen Co. of Detroit from 1947; its J-100 defines the café racer jacket, now reproduced under licence by The Real McCoy's.
Kobe maker of exacting reproductions of American military and motorcycle clothing, including the licensed Buco J-100 in vegetable-tanned horsehide.
Tostock, Suffolk firm of Steve and Edna Guylas that invented the modern quilted country jacket, supplied to the royal family.
Suffolk factory brand founded by Mrs Elliot, maker of the first nylon quilted horse rug and gilet; all garments still quilted and sewn in-house.

notes: Biker jacket rebuilt from old k49 into archetypes: Schott Perfecto (613/618/118, Beck 333), Lewis Leathers Bronx (384/440TT), Lightning 391, Buco J-100 café racer (Real McCoy's repro), Lewis Corsair 60, Vanson Model A, Langlitz Columbia. Dropped armoured/textile riding gear (Alpinestars Andes & Missile, BILT Alder 2, Dainese Rapida72, Fuel Astrail, Furygan Fighter, Merlin Barton II & Shenstone II, REV'IT! Eclipse 2, Spidi Premium, Roland Sands Truman CE) as G1 motorcycle gear per brief; dropped WORKER PLAYGROUND Grand Prix 60 (unverifiable, single-shop) and the generic unmakered 'Cafe racer jacket'/'Split-collar racer jacket' entries, which became types. Lewis Leathers duplicates (Bronx / Bronx No. 384; Super Bronx / 440TT; Universal Racer / mk2) merged. Belstaff Trialmaster and Roadmaster moved from Biker to the new Waxed cotton jacket kind; Roadmaster kept as a model only because no retrieved page gave its history. Mackintosh (named in brief for quilted) omitted: the retrieved Wikipedia page gives no quilted-jacket facts. Lightning year (1958) and Corsair year (1962) come from Lewis Leathers product pages; Buco J-100 year given as '1950s' only loosely (McCoy's page dates the Buco line to 1947 without a J-100 date) — flag to verify. No traditions added (industrial heritage makers, not artisan traditions).
